I have a query that is pretty much ran every time someone views a page on my website. It's checking the database to see if they have received a new message. If they have, it shows them a notification as well as how many messages they have in their inbox. How do you think this would handle if I were to theoretically have hundreds, or even thousands of users browsing my website? I can only assume that the server would end up getting tied up at some point. I'm not sure about how many [connections] it could withstand though.

Also, what would you recommend as the best way to go about handling this system? I know that the way I am doing it now is probably making every programmer cringe right now.
You can use Redis or Memcached for that. Since they are memory-based cache, they are faster and more efficient than regular connection.

Like @potterhere said, you'd set up something like this:

have a background job that queries your messaging table every so often and take all messages that are new/unread/whatever and place them into a redis cache. If you're not sure about redis, we can talk about that, but it's a simple no-sql style database that can interact with very simple php function. Then, in your login process, or on a timer, you can do your queries to Redis to get messages for reading purposes.

The strength of a system like this is that you can have the messages going into redis without the user logged in, because it would just be something running in the background all the time keeping the cache up-to-date.
I've never looked into Redis, but it sounds like a good way to go about this. I'll have to look into more in time.
